Subject: Competitive bakeoff recap — Redwood vs BenchAI vs NimbusEdge

Hi Samantha / Carlos —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + next steps so we all have a single source of truth. Please flag anything I missed or any reprioritization on your side.

Key pain points discussed:
- Intermittent latency spikes during peak reporting windows (p95 spikes to 800–3,200ms)
- High per-token inference cost when models are scaled to match peak throughput
- Strict data residency and audit requirements for patient PII (EU + US regional controls)
- Need for predictable SLA-backed latency for the triage assistant product

Goals / decision criteria (as discussed):
1) Latency SLO: p95 < 150ms for standard prompts under 50 tokens
2) Cost envelope: unit cost <= $0.003/token at projected monthly volume
3) Security / compliance: SOC 2 evidence + SSO (SAML/OIDC) + data residency controls
4) Operational: easy rollout path (canary/A-B), observability on token-level costs, and automated fallback for outages
5) Support & roadmap alignment (on-prem/private options a plus)

Vendors in the bakeoff we covered:
- Redwood (us) — focus on runtime latency controls, caching, and dedicated pools
- BenchAI — lightweight runtime, strong model-ops, unknowns around large-scale batching
- NimbusEdge — aggressive quantization claims, less mature observability

Open questions / items for the bakeoff tests:
- Baseline latency and p95 under our representative prompt set (we proposed your 1200-reporting prompts)
- Throughput at 500 concurrent sessions with KV-prefetching enabled
- Cache effectiveness (prefix/KV cache hit rate) on our dataset
- End-to-end security posture (SOC 2 summary, SSO test, data residency enforcement)

Attachments:
- BAKEOFF-CRITERIA.xlsx (detailed test matrix)
- Network-drawings.pdf (high-level infra)

Proposed next steps / mutual action plan:
1) Samantha: confirm final list of prompts / evaluation queries by EOD Wed 12/15 (owner: Omniva)
2) Redwood (Marissa / Aditya): deliver test plan + load-test schedule by Mon 12/13 (owner: Redwood) — attached draft test plan
3) Infra contacts: Omniva to share the point of contact for on-prem / VPN access (owner: Omniva)
4) Run vendor test window: target 12/20–12/22 (all vendors)
5) Post-test review and decision workshop: target week of 12/28

If that timeline still looks good, Aditya and I will finalize the test plan and coordinate precise windows.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—

Thanks Marissa — this is a great summary. A couple of updates from our side after we regrouped internally: security/compliance just moved to the top of the checklist — we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a working SSO integration (SAML). Also: data residency enforcement is non-negotiable for the patient PII flows, so please include a test for regional routing + any encryption-at-rest proof points.

We still want to run the latency and throughput tests, but please prioritize the security validation so we can sign off on vendor eligibility before performance tests.

Also: can you add a short test that demonstrates we can pin a model version and force a fallback to a smaller variant if availability drops? That will be used in our resiliency criteria.

Thanks Samantha — totally understand the reprioritization. We'll reorder the plan so security validation is first. Proposed adjustments and asks: 

1) Security validation (target week of 12/13–12/17):
   - Provide SOC 2 Type II summary and our SOC scope document (we will share our SOC 2 summary and the relevant controls map)
   - SSO test: we can validate SAML integration in a sandbox — need your IdP metadata and a test user (please share with Ahmed or me)
   - Data residency test: show routing to a US-only bucket and prove no egress to EU region in logs

2) Performance / functional bakeoff (target 12/20–12/22):
   - Latency p95 runs across your representative prompts
   - Throughput tests with 500 concurrent sessions and KV prefetch enabled
   - Model pin / fallback test as requested

Ask from Omniva: please share the infra contact for VPN/jumpbox access and your IdP metadata (SAML) so we can script the SSO smoke tests. We attached a short Redwood load test plan (redwood-load-test-plan.md) showing the proposed traffic profile and metrics we will capture.

If Ahmed (or the infra owner) can confirm a 2-hour maintenance/test window in the 12/20–12/22 range, we can lock dates. Rishi and I will be on-call for the tests.
